chip: Blown 13–4 lead in the first game
title: In the franchise's first game, the Milwaukee Brewers lead Detroit 13–4 in the ninth inning and lose 14–13
The St. Louis Browns win their first game, 5–2 over Cleveland
On the season's last day, Browns third baseman Red Corriden plays deep and lets Nap Lajoie bunt his way to eight hits in a doubleheader, in Lajoie's batting-title race with Ty Cobb
George Sisler gets his 257th hit of the season, a major league record that stood until 2004
George Sisler hits in his 41st straight game, an American League record until Joe DiMaggio's 56 in 1941
The Browns win Game 1 of their only World Series, 2–1 over the Cardinals
Pete Gray, who lost his right arm in a childhood accident, plays his first major league game
Hank Thompson becomes the first Black player in Browns history
Eddie Gaedel, 3 feet 7 inches tall, walks in his only plate appearance for the Browns
On Bill Veeck's Grandstand Managers' Day, fans hold up Yes and No cards to call the Browns' plays, and the Browns win 5–3
Satchel Paige, at 46, throws a 12-inning shutout to beat the Tigers 1–0
The Browns play their last game, losing 2–1 to the White Sox in 11 innings, before moving to Baltimore
The Baltimore Orioles play their first game, a 3–0 loss at Detroit
Ted Williams homers off the Orioles' Jack Fisher in the final at-bat of his career
Roger Maris hits his 59th home run off Milt Pappas at Memorial Stadium, in the Yankees' 154th game, one short of Babe Ruth's 60
Frank Robinson hits the only home run ever to leave Memorial Stadium entirely, off Cleveland's Luis Tiant
Jim Palmer, nine days short of his 21st birthday, outduels Sandy Koufax with a World Series shutout in Koufax's final game
The Miracle Mets beat the 109-win Orioles in Game 5 to take the World Series
Dave McNally hits a grand slam in Game 3, the only one by a pitcher in World Series history
Brooks Robinson is named World Series MVP after five games of diving stops at third base
Jim Palmer wins his 20th game, giving the Orioles four 20-game winners with Dave McNally, Mike Cuellar and Pat Dobson
Doug DeCinces's walk-off home run starts the summer of Orioles Magic
The Pirates win Game 7, completing a comeback from 3 games to 1 down in the World Series
Cal Ripken Jr. plays the first game of his 2,632-game streak
On the season's last day, the Brewers win 10–2 to take the AL East, and the Memorial Stadium crowd salutes the retiring Earl Weaver
Tippy Martinez picks off three Blue Jays in the 10th inning, then Lenn Sakata wins it with a home run
The Orioles beat the White Sox 9–0 for their first win, after an 0–21 start
Cal Ripken Jr. plays his 2,130th consecutive game, tying Lou Gehrig
Cal Ripken Jr. plays his 2,131st consecutive game, passing Lou Gehrig
Brady Anderson hits his 50th home run on the last day of the season
In ALCS Game 1, 12-year-old Jeffrey Maier reaches over the right-field wall to turn Derek Jeter's fly ball into a game-tying home run
Mike Mussina retires the first 25 Indians before Sandy Alomar Jr.'s single ends his perfect game bid
Cal Ripken Jr. sits out, ending his streak at 2,632 consecutive games
The Rangers beat the Orioles 30–3, the most runs by a team in a modern major league game
Down 10–1 in the seventh inning, the Orioles beat the Red Sox 11–10, the biggest comeback in Orioles history
Chris Davis hits his 51st home run, breaking Brady Anderson's franchise record
Delmon Young's pinch-hit, bases-clearing double in the eighth beats the Tigers in ALDS Game 2
The Orioles beat the White Sox 8–2 at Camden Yards with no fans allowed, after unrest in Baltimore
Edwin Encarnación's walk-off home run in the 11th ends the Wild Card Game, with Zack Britton still in the bullpen
